unitFindings.rationale: Abundance after administration is attributed to division, survival and redistribution; culture state and the administered input are assessed separately.
The blood-compartment account explicitly separates detectable sequences, viable receptor-bearing cells and useful function at the relevant site.
The added paragraph limits cellular responses to biological signalling without intention and declines benefit or safety from cell number.
Both stated fractions recompute to 20 viable receptor-positive T cells per microlitre despite the changed parent count.
Comparable collection, volume, viable gates and population definitions are explicit conditions on the arithmetic.
Sequence copies, surface receptor, viable-cell counts and functional measurements are explicitly separated.
Starting family and added receptor are separate attributes; NK and NKT are explicitly distinguished.
The fictional cards explicitly decline a product-performance inference from family or source.
Source, engineering location, administered object and native versus added recognition are carried by the source cards and family explanations.
A prepared carrier can modify the recipient's own cells; donor-derived prepared cells illustrate another source and route.
The two fictional products state administered carrier versus donor cells and identify source and location independently.
Carrier input is followed through entry, expression, survival and expansion without specifying a final in-body cell dose.
Antibody clearance, carrier exposure, instructions, protein, cells and inflammation are separate time courses.
Activity control, cell elimination, residual cells and injury reversal are distinguished and require measured performance.
The existing kinetics note states that persistent cells can prolong both useful activity and harmful recognition.
Starting-material acceptance, unsuitable cell state, nonconforming or absent lots and donor compatibility remain distinct possible failures.
The conditioning notes separate competing cells, lymphocyte and neutrophil counts, infections and whole-regimen effects.
Recipient-cell delivery and recognition of the intended antigen on healthy tissue are different steps and hazards.
The source cards answer administered object, whose cells and where engineering occurs while leaving availability and benefit unresolved.
The matched blood calculation requires valid absolute counts, parent gates and volume before expansion or loss is assigned.
The carrier card does not determine generated-cell count; the donor-cell card does not establish available supply or clinical success.
Hunter's human samples, humanised mice and monkeys remain separate; FDA development principles do not become product-efficacy results.
The board asks about accessible epitopes, negative tumour populations and actual healthy-cell recognition, beyond RNA or a disease label.
Within-lesion, between-lesion and treatment-related variation is explicit, as are differences among RNA, soluble protein, stains and finished-receptor access.
TNBC is a subtype; the board supplies recognition specifications and missing tests rather than a treatment ranking.
The universal negative is withdrawn in favour of the evidence actually read: selected preclinical work and a limited phase-I observation.
unitFindings.qualification: The curriculum universal negative is narrowed to the studies actually read; no exhaustive absence-of-benefit finding is claimed.

unitFindings.rationale: Sun's sacituzumab-derived recognition module, human-tumour work and separate murine toxicity system retain their distinct scopes.
B7-H3 synNotch induction of a TROP2 CAR is a sequential rule requiring temporal tests, not two static positive stains.
The archival tissue cohort is separated from TB129 functional testing and the actual mesothelin construct, with healthy recognition unresolved.
The new MUC1 record distinguishes cleavage-product epitopes, repeat-domain staining and RNA, retaining unresolved cleavage and noncancer staining.
Nectin4-7.19 and FAP-12 are named separately, including their cytokines, colorectal/lung models and cross-species recognition limitations.
The mAb806-derived construct is distinguished from total EGFR measurement; the tissue, culture and mouse evidence is preclinical.
R12, healthy-donor T cells, the TNBC line, scaffold and TGF-beta/SD-208 perturbation are explicitly retained.
The factor-VII light-chain module in NK-92MI, TNBC models and vascular questions remain product-specific rather than donor-NK or CAR-T results.
CD142 tissue factor is explicitly distinguished from the Thomsen-Friedenreich carbohydrate and their different study identities.
Healthy-tissue questions are requirements; sampled negative pathology or a stain is not certified as complete safe recognition.
The 70/30 accessible-antigen example explicitly contrasts an RNA result and a third-antibody healthy stain without ranking receptors.
The actual binder's functional recognition is required, including the possibility of increased recognition of healthy target-low cells.
Intended antigen on healthy tissue is distinguished from an unintended molecule; molecular specificity does not guarantee tissue selectivity.
Idealised OR/AND coverage uses the stated distribution and remains separate from killing, thresholds, timing and healthy selectivity.
Conventional TCR recognition requires a naturally processed peptide displayed by its specified HLA complex, not just source-protein expression.
Peptide binding and sequence identity are upstream of natural display and cross-reactivity testing; an intracellular source can yield a surface complex.
The named label retains autologous MAGE-A4 peptide-HLA therapy, its specified HLA alleles and synovial-sarcoma population.
Sun's human tumour experiments and human-TROP2/murine-cell injury comparison are explicitly distinct and not human safety estimates.
Induction, receptor persistence after priming, tissue movement and residual healthy recognition are stated as temporal tests.
Missed negative cells, inaccessible intracellular signals, post-treatment variation and inflammatory conditions remain recognition questions.
The worked explanation requires epitope, tumour distribution, healthy recognition and model/time context rather than an antigen name.
The retained Morgan account specifies receptor, dose and conditioning, and labels the normal-lung mechanism as the authors' single-case hypothesis.
FDA specificity and functional healthy-recognition recommendations are carried as development principles, without claiming the board's products passed them.
The cell, its genetic instructions and the receptor protein are explicitly three different objects.
The instruction-to-surface-to-contact sequence is explained in prose, with shapes and arrows kept schematic rather than evidence of completed killing.
DNA-template transcription and message translation are defined separately; delivered mRNA starts at translation and later processing remains necessary.
Folding and membrane trafficking occur downstream of sequence detection; DNA positivity leaves functional display unresolved.
Conventional peptide-HLA recognition and accessible-surface-antigen CAR recognition are distinguished without erasing the cell's other inputs.
The actual binder and epitope, finished format and unwanted recognition need assessment separately from purified binding.
The hinge comparison retains expression and cell-contact geometry; Hudecek does not establish universally superior spacer length.
The transmembrane region is assessed for assembly, surface expression and interactions rather than assumed to be a neutral peg.
Baseline signalling, repeated encounters and completed target-cell killing are distinct tests, beyond binding or surface expression.
The frozen peer fields define paired-domain scFv and single-domain VHH architectures and explicitly decline a performance hierarchy.
unitFindings.qualification: Architecture is carried in frozen PR-373 fields, not a newly integrated root owner.

unitFindings.rationale: Hudecek's R11/spacer constraint and Fc-interaction findings remain particular construct and animal observations.
Activation and borrowed costimulatory regions are parts within the receptor, rather than independently administered medicines.
Kawalekar's central-memory/respiratory and effector-memory/glycolytic findings retain their human-cell construct scope and reject clinical rankings.
Other receptor parts, starting-cell state, preparation, target and disease are retained when comparing domains.
First-, second- and third-generation labels describe activation plus zero, one or two added costimulatory regions, not quality scores.
Ramos's separately tracked co-infused products have measured kinetics without isolation of either product's contribution to shared tumour response.
Kymriah's label supplies autologous CD19 targeting, murine scFv, CD8 structural segments and 4-1BB/CD3-zeta domains.
The CD8-derived hinge/anchor is separated from the cell population; the label permits other cell populations.
Shared parts or autologous source do not transfer the labelled product's outcomes to another construct.
DNA positivity without killing leaves RNA, folding, trafficking, binding and signalling open before a stronger binder is selected.
Misfolding, unstimulated signalling, geometry and healthy recognition are separate failures despite a receptor-positive assay.
The matched hinge exercise preserves purified binding while asking about surface expression and cellular contact geometry.
Simultaneous second-/third-generation infusion and separate kinetics are carried without assigning a shared clinical response to either product.
Experimental design studies, a named product description and a small clinical comparison retain separate evidence levels.
Engineering outside the body followed by cell infusion is contrasted with administering an instruction carrier that generates modified cells inside.
Cytosolic mRNA translation and nuclear DNA-template transcription are explained alongside omitted entry/release steps and separate functional evidence.
Source and engineering location do not prove absence of conditioning, quality testing or monitoring requirements.
Removing individual cell culture leaves carrier manufacture, quality decisions, traceability and recipient readiness unresolved for the actual programme.
Leukapheresis is variable starting material; total collection is not necessarily an adequate viable T-cell input or an accepted lot.
Expansion, selection and activation affect different attributes; a larger count does not establish functional quality or unchanged composition.
Post-preservation viability/function, identity/custody and relevant potency remain separate manufacturing questions.
Collection-to-infusion time includes handling, testing and clinical readiness, while completed manufacture and eventual infusion use different denominators.
The source change does not remove identity tracking, stability assessment, release decisions or comparability after process changes.
The particle's recipient-cell address is separated from the encoded effector's recognition target and downstream safety.
Carrier, payload, transduction, integration and expression are defined as distinct stages rather than equivalent permanent modification.
Usable mRNA delivery reaches the cytosol; RNA, receptor protein, cells and activity need separate duration measurements.
Lentiviral RNA-to-DNA, integration and subsequent transcription are distinct from survival, expression, unintended-cell and insertion effects.
AAV nuclear delivery and often episomal persistence retain tissue/division/integration qualifications rather than universal genetic-fate labels.
The cassette/transposase pair requires delivery, and the resulting nonviral system can integrate.
Integration-deficient and self-inactivating lentiviral designs are explicitly different; disabling LTR regulation does not prevent integration.
The targeted-LNP paragraph separates temporary message exposure from an editor's lasting DNA alteration.
Carrier names do not fix administration route; the lipoplex vaccine's APC targeting is not T-cell engineering evidence.
Rurik's mouse cardiac-injury/FAP example remains distinct from human or cancer efficacy.
The Sleeping Beauty report concerns electroporated cells expanded ex vivo and then infused, not direct injection of components.
Hunter's cell samples, humanised-tumour mice and monkey B-cell depletion remain distinct nonclinical experiments.
Frank's abstract does not verify the specified stem-cell-derived model, complete vector and sampled compartments; no detailed new claim is adopted.
The exact Frank T/non-T/mouse parent gates remain source-open because the accessible abstract does not carry them.
Frank's detailed peak/decline, controls and per-animal baseline are not verified by the accessible abstract and receive no coverage credit.
Pfeiffer's activated-human-cell NSG model, separate lymphoma conditions and vehicle/reporter controls are carried explicitly.
Day-seven compartment percentages are verified, but the CD8-negative parent population cannot yet be narrowed to T cells without the supplementary gate.
unitFindings.qualification: The source Results says CD8-negative cells; the more specific T-cell parent gate requires Appendix Fig S1A. Supplement retrieval timed out or returned HTML instead of a valid DOCX. Only the verified broader wording is carried.

unitFindings.rationale: B-cell depletion, CAR expression, initial B-cell supply and antigen-driven expansion are separate measurements rather than entry-efficiency estimates.
The experiments retain model, activation state, time, compartment and comparator without claiming a completed human efficacy/safety chain.
Administered carrier/RNA is not the final count or identity of generated cells; the chain asks what entered and became expressed.
Every stage from administered carrier to exposure, entry/release, expression, cell fate, movement and target effects is carried separately.
Fluorescent uptake does not establish usable expression, and two population-level detections do not establish same-cell coexpression.
A carrier aliquot, timed blood and tissue biopsy sample different material and do not count every cell or organ.
Sequence copies, viable gated fractions and controlled killing remain separate readouts with specimen and denominator context.
Thresholds and controls are product-specific; the explicitly ex vivo-focused FDA guidance does not validate an in vivo carrier specification.
Failed entry/release, unsuitable state, unintended recipient cells and unsafe healthy-antigen recognition are distinct possible failures.
The ex vivo/in vivo definition explicitly distinguishes an animal test of infused engineered cells from cell generation inside the animal.
Carrier quality and downstream engineered-cell function remain different potency questions after cell culture is removed.
The 60/200, 5/100 and 60/65 fractions are recomputed with their respective denominators and explicitly do not establish exclusive delivery.
Matched receptor, antigen-positive/-negative and relevant healthy-cell controls are required before interpreting recognition effects.
Delivery address, therapeutic recognition and genetic fate are explained with the missing model, time, population or function kept visible.
Muscle AAV persistence, the NPG-mouse lentiviral example and risk-based follow-up remain separate tissue/model/regulator scopes.
Recognition, signalling support and target-cell killing are separate jobs; the added feature does not confer a safe target or patient benefit.
The receptor/support/CAR scenes are explained as intended signalling arrangements and hypothetical assay results, rather than measured clinical improvements.
Cytokines are receptor-dependent signalling proteins, not nutritional fuel; exposure and receiving-cell state shape the possible response.
The IL-2 paragraph explicitly includes regulatory and other responding T cells and confines Boyman's formulation findings to mice.
The new pathway note names JAK-STAT as one cytokine route, separates a SMAD-associated response and keeps pathway signals distinct from phenotype.
Engelowski's artificial ligands, receptors and experimental signalling/growth are specified without claiming completed killing or human control.
Drug-gated support requires baseline, exposure and withdrawal tests, beyond a nominal switch design.
Antigen-triggered support requires tests after cells leave the triggering site and after priming ends.
Constitutive signalling raises growth and state questions rather than guaranteeing useful support.
Secreted payloads can affect neighbours or circulation; the design does not guarantee intracellular confinement.
Orthogonality is conditional on measured partner selectivity, and the supportive receptor is distinguished from CAR targeting and secretion.
The dominant-negative receptor is a signalling-interfering variant, distinct from a gene deletion or removal of all suppression.
Narayan's prostate-cancer phase-I complete product retains severe CRS and concurrent sepsis, without isolating the armour's causal effect.
TRUCK terminology is expanded and universal is explicitly a historical name rather than universal tumour recognition.
IL-12/macrophage effects on antigen-loss cells belong to the model and do not change the CAR binder's target.
Zhang's IL-12-producing metastatic-melanoma TILs and systemic toxicity are distinguished from the earlier CAR/TRUCK model.
NFAT/activation responsiveness is not tumour-exclusive secretion; production, distribution and systemic effects require separate evidence.
AND/OR/NOT inputs and two independently activating CARs are distinguished, rather than calling any two targets an AND gate.
Sequential priming, induced CAR decay and movement between sites retain a temporal state rather than same-cell simultaneous positivity.
Kloss's tuned activation/costimulation and Roybal's induction system remain distinct tested designs, not universal logic-label results.
The equal-input 100/250-cell, 20/25-per-cent killing and 2/18-per-cent injury observations are retained as fictional separate assays.
The count ratio is 2.5; division, survival and loss remain unresolved and the ratio is not a treatment-benefit ratio.
The mixed tumour/healthy-cell findings retain their denominators and uncertainty without defining a body-wide safety window.
Baseline activity, persistent trigger exposure, altered cell states and healthy recognition remain different failures of the support hypothesis.
Signal reduction, retained viable cells, continued CAR function and injury reversal are separate observations and interventions.
Each added feature is a hypothesis with function, failure tests and finished-product context, rather than a guaranteed improvement.
The review framework, preclinical designs and distinct early clinical products are kept at their actual evidence levels.
Entry, recognition, useful function and healthy-tissue harm are separate links; more cells do not establish a complete treatment chain.
Movement toward a site and entry through tissue are distinguished, as are blood abundance, biopsy sampling and vessel count versus perfusion.
Vessels, matrix and local signals are possible context variables; a low cell count alone does not identify the limiting cause.
Within-/between-lesion and temporal heterogeneity is retained, and RNA does not specify the receptor-accessible surface feature.
The escape account retains unrecognised populations and changes without attributing intention to cancer or cells.
Conventional CAR surface-target dependence is separated from peptide-HLA dependency and from changes in induced versus baseline display.
Hypoxia, nutrients, inhibitory inputs and chronic stimulation remain distinct hypotheses; exhaustion is a cell-state concept rather than physical fatigue.
Inhibitory-marker expression and suppressor-cell counts are explicitly insufficient to assign a causal input or blockade benefit.
Adenosine generation/receptors and intracellular IDO tryptophan metabolism are separate routes; composition does not demonstrate suppression.
The support notes separate detectable persistence from useful function and do not infer oxygen, access or missing antigen from more signalling.
Chen's endogenous-promoter payload work remains a cell/mouse design, separate from generating cells by in vivo carrier delivery.
Healthy intended-antigen injury, unintended binding, CRS and neurologic syndromes are separate outcomes requiring their own functional and clinical observations.
The fictional 80/20 population leaves 20 survivors; added effector number does not create their absent antigen.
A complex-model functional contrast calls for controlled tests and does not assign a macrophage, vessel or pathway mechanism.
The specified overlap sums to 100, with OR coverage of 90 and AND coverage of 20 under idealised recognition assumptions.
Recognition coverage is explicitly not observed killing, tissue access, useful cell state or healthy-tissue selectivity.
The actual epitope/receptor and healthy-recognition questions remain attached when moving from binding to tissue and functional measurements.
A working binder, scarce tumour-biopsy cells and possible healthy recognition leave distribution, function and safety independently unresolved.
Targeted instruction delivery and therapeutic recognition have different addresses; the carrier does not make an antigen cancer-exclusive.
An additional target can expand candidate coverage, while neither its logic label nor a support signal establishes safe access or function.
Improved abundance or trafficking does not show retained function, and switching a signal or cells does not undo established injury.
Rising blood counts and sparse biopsies raise sampling/distribution questions before more expansion is selected as the solution.
The broad absence claims are narrowed to the actual preclinical and early human evidence rather than certified from selected products.
unitFindings.qualification: No global absence of breast indications or clinical benefit is inferred from a selected product list.

unitFindings.rationale: The ROR1 trial retains 21 total, three CLL, ten TNBC, eight NSCLC and one response among 18 pooled solid-tumour participants.
A TNBC subtype or pipeline listing does not specify a receptor target, clinical indication, availability or benefit.
The worked explanation follows access, recognition, function and harm and asks which link each proposed change actually tested.
NCI mechanism discussion, preclinical payload engineering, phase-I ROR1 observations and consensus taxonomy remain distinct evidence types.
Recipient-cell delivery, intended-antigen healthy recognition, unintended molecular binding, systemic inflammation and delayed genetic effects are separate causal questions.
The actual receptor's functional healthy-cell recognition is required; a tissue stain alone cannot establish injury or safety.
Cross-reactivity tests and natural-target tests are distinct, with affinity or an expression signal insufficient to establish specificity.
Onset, maximum grade, organ effects, intervention and follow-up are separate safety observations in the clinical reporting notes.
ICANS needs clinical assessment, a named framework and alternative-cause review, not an immune marker or cell count.
Conditioning, prior treatment and the whole regimen retain blood-count, infection, duration and organ-risk questions.
Genetic fate and unintended recipient cells require persistence and delayed follow-up evidence, beyond short-term tumour control.
Staining, controlled healthy-cell effects, animal evidence and clinical injury remain separate tiers with species and observation limits.
CRS and ICANS have distinct assessments and timelines; recovery of one does not establish recovery of the other.
The new paragraph names the 2026 abstract-level framework while the retained detailed clinical criteria remain explicitly 2019.
All five added 2026 groupings and T-cell-engager scope are named; timing alone is not diagnostic evidence.
Lymphocytes, neutrophils and infections are distinct, with severity, recovery, previous therapy and regimen contributions retained.
The existing CRS explanation explicitly rejects cytokine-payload absence as protection, and marker/cell changes do not establish organ recovery.
Monitoring intent, interventions actually given and later outcomes are distinguished without inferring causal efficacy from sequence.
FDA recommendations remain development/monitoring principles, whereas the paper supplies the clinical interventions actually observed.
The report's treated cancers, receptor-fusion architecture, historical cutoff and two grading frameworks remain separate from other products.
The treated denominator, CRS grade counts and one self-limited ICANS observation are retained exactly.
Amendment INV-01 corrects the frozen paraphrase: six days (1–55) is CRS duration, not onset; treatment and follow-up counts remain exact.
unitFindings.qualification: INV-01: the frozen paraphrase mislabels six days (1–55) as onset. The source and new reader correctly call this duration; onset was three days (0–9). The report’s follow-up wording is retained alongside its early fatal events and does not imply that all participants survived for 12 weeks.

unitFindings.rationale: No unreported bedside rationale, ICANS treatment or monitoring schedule is supplied, and recovery is not a randomised intervention effect.
Activity regulation and selective cell elimination are different, with residual functions, loss of therapy and irreversible injury considered separately.
Di Stasi's ages, donor cells, haploidentical transplant and GVHD context are specified rather than treated as universal CAR rescue evidence.
Switch expression, trigger tissue reach, response time, surviving/regrowing cells and access to drug and specialist care are separate requirements.
The 100-to-five reduction is 95 per cent in matched blood; a lower cytokine result and unchanged injury remain different outcomes.
Surviving viable cells, tissue coverage, time and retained function remain explicit after a relative count reduction.
Insertion, consequential gene effects, clonal expansion and malignancy are explicitly distinct observations requiring causal investigation.
Both integrating lentiviral and transposon designs are described; nonviral is not a clinical safety ranking.
ABECMA's warning is confined to its autologous BCMA/CD19 blood-cancer context and lifelong monitoring, without a new experimental incidence claim.
Hamilton's single-centre count and lethal lymphoma retain the axi-cel gammaretroviral identity and absence of evidence for oncogenic integration in that case.
Persistent or delayed effects are assessed by product risk, not one identical follow-up requirement for every carrier.
Untested healthy recognition, incomplete switch reach and short follow-up remain separate weaknesses despite favourable surrogate results.
Six people observed for four weeks cannot prove zero risk or validate an untested rescue mechanism.
The worked explanation separates the measured harm, tested control, time and remaining uncertainty rather than equating lower signal with safety.
Consensus categories, a product warning, regulator recommendations and causal mechanistic findings retain their own scopes and reading limits.
Signal, dish killing, tissue distribution and whole-body safety remain different claims rather than a single efficacy result.
The carrier-product definition and ex vivo/in vivo distinction require identifying what was administered, not the experiment's animal location alone.
The explicitly fictional nonclinical cards cannot supply a human trial or comparative clinical-benefit result.
Product, antigen, source, setting and comparator remain attached; missing evidence cannot be borrowed from another product's success.
The packet defines carrier, RNA, extracellular epitope/CAR, trigger/support receptor and absence of cell-elimination machinery.
One T-cell donor, selected human model components, technical wells and lot-specific functional versus identity evidence are carried separately.
The stated same-carrier/total-RNA comparator and D-present, D-absent and D-alone controls remain limited to the supplied experiments.
The 24-hour cell table retains all 1,000/100, 60/240, 50/150 and 40 counts with unexposed negative controls.
All four fractions use their own parent population: 50, 25, 20 and 40 per cent respectively.
RNA, surface display and same-cell dual expression are explicitly distinct and do not establish killing or whole-body specificity.
The 48-hour 80/55/50/5 killing observations retain 100 target cells, matched controls and three technical wells from one donor.
The matched assay supports a conditional R/D-associated contribution but supplies neither independent donors nor an uncertainty interval.
The healthy-organoid card retains 48 hours, D in both arms, 90/95 survival, two organoid donors and one T-cell donor.
The five-point difference has no supplied threshold or uncertainty and is not a body-wide safety window.
The mouse card retains administered P versus empty carrier, D in both arms, six mice and no CAR-without-R arm.
The selected blood fraction is 120/200 at day seven, distinct from arm size; only two treated biopsies were sampled.
The 300/1,000 contrast is 70 per cent smaller than control but three times the 100 baseline, not regression or cure.
The group comparison does not isolate R, explain poor infiltration, establish later durability or describe every animal.
Identity in B/C cannot transfer lot A's function; three lots are not three independent biological donors or evidence of post-storage potency.
At 24 hours after withdrawal the signal falls 100 to 20 against continued D at 100, while 90 of 100 cells remain in one donor's technical wells.
Reduced R-associated signal is not cell elimination, absence of CAR recognition or reversal of injury.
The missing human study supplies no clinical denominator; missing evidence is explicitly not a zero-per-cent event rate.
Person-level study-defined objective response is explicitly distinct from the fraction of target cells killed in culture.
Each card retains its product, specimen, controls, denominator, time and uncertainty and asks for the next missing measurement.
The 100/1,000/10,000 logarithmic marks are tenfold ratios, not additive steps or evidence of regression.
The cards expose gaps between expression, control, lot identity and animal effects; they do not join into an unmeasured clinical causal chain.
The connected explanation answers product identity, matched controls, each denominator and outstanding human/safety questions without treating invented data as evidence.
FDA product-characterisation and functional-development principles frame the reasoning without validating fictional P or a numerical release threshold.
Family, donor/recipient origin, engineering location and administered object are independent attributes rather than a patient-benefit hierarchy.
Conventional CAR recognition requires its accessible surface target and product-specific healthy-recognition evidence.
Conventional alpha-beta TCR-T requires its naturally processed displayed peptide and compatible retained HLA complex.
TIL manufacture starts from tumour-derived cells with existing receptors and variable selection/mixture, not an assumed added receptor.
The added CAR is one NK input; native activation/inhibition, source, support and preparation retain separate evidence requirements.
Gamma-delta recognition varies by subset and receptor; phosphoantigen/nonclassical and HLA-restricted examples defeat a universal HLA-free label.
NK and NKT are distinguished and family identity does not establish an efficacy, safety or persistence ranking.
Paired coding chains, finished-cell expression, native population/mixture, actual recognition and healthy testing are separate checks.
Simoni's bystanders and the TIL manufacturing notes separate infiltration, useful tumour reactivity and a manufacturable infusion product.
Liu's particular IL-15/switch cord-blood product shows why neither short persistence nor broad family safety can be inferred universally.
Matched engineered/unmodified effectors and target-positive/-negative cells test antigen dependence rather than expression alone.
The TCR validation paragraph requires removal/restoration of antigen/HLA with viable matched targets before dependency is assigned.
Changing a relevant native NK ligand tests one input, with target viability and other ligand changes controlled.
Gamma-delta testing compares native and added routes with receptor blockade or target perturbation and matched healthy controls.
Activation, cytokine or granule release and completed killing remain distinct; a perturbation does not identify every possible recognition route.
Loss of one allele is distinguished from shared class-I B2M dependency, while class-II alpha/beta composition is explicitly different.
Reduced class-I inhibition does not guarantee NK killing; a conventional CAR retains target, access, function and safety requirements.
A target or cell-family name does not inherit another product's clinical performance or availability.
Loss of A does not establish B-restricted recognition without the corresponding peptide/display, or validate another CAR route.
One antigen-negative line does not show escape prevention; native ligand, healthy recognition and clinical context remain untested.
The receptor-transfer explanation asks for type, paired chains, target/peptide-HLA and functional testing rather than a generic installation claim.
The tumour-origin explanation asks about identities, mixture, selection and actual reactivity, rather than calling every recovered cell tumour-specific.
The CAR-NK explanation retains added and native inputs and explicitly declines comparative benefit or access from sparse family descriptions.
The worked explanation uses family, source, engineered change and perturbation tests with unresolved safety and clinical evidence.
Morgan's receptor-transfer study, Simoni's infiltrate observations and Liu's cord-blood product remain separate experiments and populations.
The study paragraph states product, treated cancers, design, reviewer, cutoff, confirmation rule and participant denominators before its response fractions.
Product recognition and participant flow are reconstructed independently; a receptor-fusion name is not a clinical outcome.
Collection, completed/conforming lots, treatment and imaging/evaluability are separated, and noninfusion is not automatically manufacturing failure.
Initial and confirmed responses are separated, as are their assessor/cutoff, response duration, survival and quality of life.
The report is historical single-arm phase-I dose escalation within a phase-I/II programme, rather than a current approval/access claim.
Autologous ex vivo antibody/CD3-epsilon fusion recognises surface mesothelin without the conventional peptide-HLA dependency.
The actual treated cancers are mesothelioma, ovarian cancer and cholangiocarcinoma, without extrapolating a comparator or another disease benefit.
The phase-I intent-to-treat group is 48 consented/apheresed, against 32 infused and 30 response-evaluable people.
The numerator distinguishes six centrally reviewed responses from four confirmed partial responses.
Two grade-5 events preceded post-infusion imaging; missing scans neither rule out harm nor establish causation.
The six responses give 20 per cent of 30 or 12.5 per cent of 48; four confirmed responses give about 13.3 per cent of 30.
The single-arm result does not estimate comparative, durable or cross-disease benefit.
Assessor, time, confirmation and population stay attached, and the 32-person safety denominator is not replaced by 30 response-evaluable people.
A historical data cutoff and source-check date explicitly do not establish recruitment, approval, availability or personal eligibility.
The unchanged observations are recalculated under 30 versus 48 denominators rather than silently changing the population.
The worked explanation supplies mechanism, population, flow and response rule and identifies the unresolved comparison.
The raw Hassan report and targeted participant-flow/safety passages support the ledger rather than a generic trial definition or educational route.
The administered carrier/cells, source, engineering site and later living-cell behaviour are distinguished without a fixed generated-cell dose.
Recognition, supportive/logic design and tissue context remain connected questions rather than proof of a safe complete product.
The evidence-reading paragraphs retain comparator, model, time and population before any preclinical or clinical inference.
Ex vivo/in vivo alternatives converge on measured cells, tissue entry, harm and outcome questions; the route map is not a validated protocol.
DNA, RNA, receptor protein, cell family and activation/costimulation are separate concepts and functions.
Conventional TCRs contact a surface peptide-HLA complex, not the intact intracellular source protein.
Native tumour-derived repertoires, added receptors and native NK/gamma-delta inputs remain distinct without a strategy ranking.
The frozen peer fields distinguish binder architecture/soluble-size consequences from affinity, epitope, developability and complete-product function.
unitFindings.qualification: Binder-format/profile content depends on frozen peer PR-373 fields; no new root record or duplicate is created.

unitFindings.rationale: Added obstacle-directed functions, coverage logic, control mechanisms and cytokine context are separate design questions.
Tissue context, escape of unrecognised populations and altered cell state remain distinct possible failures.
Source, location, delivery targeting and therapeutic recognition are separated; actual vector designs determine integration and persistence questions.
GMP quality systems, one-lot disposition, relevant biological activity and comparability after changes retain distinct scopes.
Conditioning risks, separate acute syndromes and risk-based delayed-genetic assessment are not replaced by a CAR assay.
Preclinical/engineering promise and selected blood-cancer success do not establish comparative solid-tumour benefit.
The in vivo route does not prove easier reversal, less toxicity or a complete clinically useful product.
The original-only route retains candidate discovery/testing, recognition versus connected action and a profile retested in the assembled format.
unitFindings.qualification: The original-only route combines an existing root discovery field with frozen peer targeting/profile fields; peer status is retained.

unitFindings.rationale: The original-only route distinguishes a cytokine medicine, a measured signal and an engineered cytokine-producing cell.
The original-only route preserves collection, expansion, material/recipient identity, cold handling, relevant potency and process comparability.
The later-only universal B2M claim is corrected to the actual shared class-I dependency, with class-II alpha/beta components separate.

unitFindings.rationale: Source is distinct from engineering site, and donor-to-recipient attack versus host rejection remain two conditional incompatibility directions.
Collection-to-infusion interval and never-infused people are distinguished from culture time through the actual 48/32/30 ledger.
The immediate-use ex vivo sterility example retains the named testing approach and later-result plan, without universal post-infusion release timing.
The later-only healthy-recognition example explicitly shows why a perfectly specific binder can injure intended-antigen healthy tissue.
